div.head: Hn Lond 7
div.ab: Et homo Londoñ. non iudicetur in misericordia pecunie nisi a sa were, scilicet ad C solidos: dico de placito quod ad pecuniam pertineat.
Et homo Lond. non iudicetur in misericordia pecuniae nisi ad sa were, scilicet ad C solidos; dico de placito quod ad pecuniam pertineat.
And a citizen of London shall not be sentenced to forfeiture of a sum greater than his wergeld, namely 100 shillings, that is to say in a case concerned with monetary compensation.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 290–291 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 525, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: ad Cc Horn Cust El E IV; in Whel.
ad Cc Horn Cust El E IV; in Whel.

Die Krone verzichtet auf unbegrenzte Misericordia (s. d. Gl 3) von Bürgern wie von Kronvassallen CHn cor 8. Ebenso wie hier lautet der Freibrief mit demselben Maximum (Wergeld) für Colchester 1189; Bateson EHR 1901, 94; Ballard 151. Dass das Strafgeld höchstens Wergeld (s. d. Gl 27) betrage, ist ein das 12. Jh. überdauernder Rest des Agsächs. Systems

The Crown renounces unlimited misericordia (see that word in Gl 3) from burgesses, as from its vassals in CHn cor 8. The charter for Colchester of 1189 is worded just as here, with the same maximum (wergild); Bateson EHR 1901, 94; Ballard 151. That the fine should amount at most to the wergild (see that word in Gl 27) is a survival of the Anglo-Saxon system that outlasted the 12th cent.

Benutzt von Lib. Lond 3, 1. Dagegen sagt dafür secundum legem civitatis der Freibrief von 1155.—Das à bed. ‘bis zur Höhe von’, nicht ‘in’.—Über des Londoners 5 £-Wergeld s. d. Gl 5, auch Bateson EHR 1902, 484. 492. 495. 707. 709. 721.—Weit geringer war des Strafgelds (s. d. Gl 1a. 17) Maximum, das Heinrich I. dem Newcastler setzte: 6 Ör = ¹/₂ £; die Bürger von Battle haben ein Strafmaximum von 2¹/₂ £; Davis EHR 1914, 428

Used by Lib. Lond 3, 1. The charter of 1155, on the other hand, says secundum legem civitatis instead.—The à means ‘up to the amount of’, not ‘in’.—On the Londoner’s wergild of 5 £ see that word in Gl 5, also Bateson EHR 1902, 484. 492. 495. 707. 709. 721.—Far lower was the maximum fine (see that word in Gl 1a. 17) that Henry I set for the burgess of Newcastle: 6 ores = ¹/₂ £; the burgesses of Battle have a maximum fine of 2¹/₂ £; Davis EHR 1914, 428
Bussloses (s. d. Gl 1c. 3), mit Leibesstrafe Bedrohtes, fällt also ausdrücklich nicht unter diesen Satz
Offences not admitting of compensation (see that word in Gl 1c. 3), which are threatened with corporal punishment, are therefore expressly excluded from this provision
